Iohn Bapti{{ls}}t.}}cour{{ls}}e of Abia: and his vvife of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=6}} And they vvere both {{sup|‖}} iu{{ls}}t before God, vvalking {{sup|‖}} in al the commaundements and {{sup|‖}} iu{{ls}}tifications of our Lord vvithout blame, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=7}} and they had no {{ls}}onne: for that Elizabeth vvas barren, and both vvere vvel {{ls}}triken in their daies. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=8}} And it came to pa{{ls}}{{ls}}e: vvhen he executed the prie{{ls}}tly function in the order of his cour{{ls}}e before God, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=9}} according to the cu{{ls}}tome of the Prie{{ls}}tly function, he vvent forth by lot {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 3, 17.''}}* to offer incen{{ls}}e, entring into the temple of our Lord: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=10}} and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 16, 16.''}}* al the multitude of the people vvas {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We {{ls}}ee here that the Prie{{ls}}t did his dutie within, the people in the meane time praying without: and that the Prie{{ls}}ts functions did profite then, though they neither heard nor {{ls}}aw his doings.}}∷ praying vvithout at the houre of the incen{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=11}} And there appeared to him an Angel of our<noinclude>{{continues|Lord,}}</noinclude>
